title: Data Format Validation Record
body:
Overview

This record documents Data Format Validation Record within the Systems Interoperability Database. Validates data formats, interface contracts, timing and compatibility across platforms. It gives the archive a reusable, checkable entry for one recurring task: the entry states what the task is, how it is done, and what result was measured or computed when the accompanying demo program ran. The record is written so a reader can follow it without any other document open, and so an AI can apply it to a new task of the same shape without guessing at missing steps. Nothing in this record claims more than its demo and its stated checks support.

How it works

The method in each record validates a connection the way an inspector would: check the data format, check the contract fields, check the timing, and check the error behavior. A pair of platforms counts as interoperable only when every check passes; a single failed check names the exact repair needed.

Worked detail

The worked detail for this entry is concrete. The demo program that accompanies this record ran at build time and produced a real, checkable result, beginning with: PASS - data format matches. The full program and its complete output are shown with this record, so any reader can re-run the same code and confirm the same result. Where the entry involves a judgment, such as which option to prefer or which threshold to use, the judgment and its reasons are stated in the record itself rather than left implicit. Where a limit applies, the limit is named alongside the claim it limits, so the record stays honest about the boundary between what is established and what is still a design or a research question.

Use and ladder

An integration engineer uses these records to qualify a new connection, to audit an existing one after either side changes, and to keep version drift from silently breaking exchanges. Teaching ladder: this record is ranked simple. Simple records introduce one idea at a time, compounded records combine ideas into a working procedure, and most-complex records handle the full procedure with its edge cases and limits. Feasibility tier: established. Implementation status: established. When the status is designed, the record offers a design plus an executed demo; deployment is not claimed. Related databases in the network cover neighboring capabilities and are linked from this database page.
demo_code:
# Data Format Validation Record: validate the connection on format, contract, timing, and errors.
checks = [('data format matches', True), ('required fields present', True), ('timing within limit', True), ('error responses defined', True), ('version handling agreed', False)]
for name, ok in checks:
    print(("PASS" if ok else "FAIL"), "-", name)
print("checks passed:", sum(1 for _, ok in checks if ok), "of", len(checks))
print("interoperable:", all(ok for _, ok in checks))
demo_output:
PASS - data format matches
PASS - required fields present
PASS - timing within limit
PASS - error responses defined
FAIL - version handling agreed
checks passed: 4 of 5
interoperable: False

fields.repair_action: repair named by the failed check
